spec: Build a bookmark manager API protected by an API key. The API key is stored in AWS Secrets Manager, and every request must present it in a header. Users can save bookmarks with a URL, title and tags, list bookmarks filtered by tag, and delete bookmarks. Bookmarks are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Adds secret-backed API-key enforcement and tag filtering to a bookmark store.

congruence_checklist: Secrets Manager secret holding the API key
GET endpoint filtering bookmarks by tag

plan.summary: A FastAPI service that manages personal bookmarks (URL, title, tags) persisted in DynamoDB. Every request must present a shared API key in the X-API-Key header; the expected key is fetched from AWS Secrets Manager at startup (cached, with refresh on mismatch). Clients can create bookmarks, list them with optional tag filtering, fetch a single bookmark, and delete bookmarks. No asynchronous or event-driven processing is implied, so no Lambda/SQS/SNS resources are planned.

endpoints.purpose: Unauthenticated liveness probe used by the harness to confirm the service is up and can reach its dependencies.
Create a bookmark from a JSON body containing url, title and optional tags; stores the item in DynamoDB and returns the created record with its generated id.
List bookmarks, optionally filtered by an exact tag via the ?tag= query parameter; supports simple pagination via limit.
Retrieve a single bookmark by id, returning 404 if it does not exist.
Delete a bookmark by id, returning 404 if it does not exist and 204 on success.

data_models.name: Bookmark
fields: tags: list[string] (default empty list, lowercased and de-duplicated)

data_models.name: BookmarkListResponse
fields: tag: string | null (echo of the applied filter)

aws_resources.name: bookmarks
aws_resources.justification: Primary store for bookmark records; partition key bookmark_id (S). The application writes on POST, reads on GET/list, and deletes on DELETE. Tag filtering is served by a GSI on the tag attribute where feasible, otherwise a filtered scan.

aws_resources.name: bookmarks-tag-index (GSI on table 'bookmarks')
aws_resources.justification: Global secondary index keyed on tag (S) + bookmark_id (S) so that GET /bookmarks?tag=... can query rather than scan; the app writes one index-friendly tag projection per bookmark.

aws_resources.name: bookmark-manager/api-key
aws_resources.justification: Holds the shared API key JSON ({"api_key": "..."}). The app calls GetSecretValue at startup and on cache expiry to validate the X-API-Key header on every request.

aws_resources.name: bookmark-manager-app-role (+ policy bookmark-manager-app-policy)
aws_resources.justification: Grants the running service dynamodb:PutItem/GetItem/DeleteItem/Query/Scan on the bookmarks table and its index, secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the API key secret, and CloudWatch Logs write permissions.

aws_resources.name: /cloudforge/bookmark-manager-api
aws_resources.justification: Log group for application request/error logs emitted by the service, giving operational visibility for auth failures and DynamoDB errors.

assumptions: The API key header name is X-API-Key; a missing header returns 401 and a wrong key returns 403 (401 also acceptable), with /health left unauthenticated so the harness can probe readiness.
The secret is stored as JSON with an 'api_key' field, but the app also accepts a raw plaintext secret string for robustness.
This is a single-tenant/shared-key API: bookmarks are not partitioned per user, since the spec mentions no user accounts or per-user identity.
Tag filtering matches a single exact tag (case-insensitive, tags normalised to lowercase on write); multi-tag or substring search is out of scope.
bookmark_id is a server-generated uuid4 string; clients cannot supply their own id.
DynamoDB uses PAY_PER_REQUEST billing, which LocalStack accepts, and no update endpoint is provided because the spec only lists save, list and delete.
AWS endpoints are configured via environment variables (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_REGION, table and secret names) so the service can target LocalStack.
No asynchronous processing, notifications, file uploads or scheduled jobs are required, so SQS, SNS, S3, Lambda and API Gateway are deliberately omitted.
